description:
## Background

Focused Graph deliberately omits closed Issues that are not needed as direct context. Users also need an explicit way to inspect the complete Current Workspace without confusing that dense view with the default. Scope is navigation state: Back and Forward must restore whether an entry showed Focused or every Issue.

This repository is the representative dense case recorded in the Graph plan: 141 Issues and 213 relationship links were observed on 2026-09-18. Scale is not a production constraint, but the complete graph must remain usable at that size.

Triage: ready-for-agent.

## What to build

Add Show all scope to Graph Mode. Users can switch between Focused and every Issue, see accurate scope counts, and have navigation restore the exact scope.

## Technical Approach

- Support `/graph?scope=all` as the complete graph route and canonicalize missing/default scope to Focused.
- Extend the Graph navigation entry so scope is validated, serialized, recorded, labeled, and restored through Back/Forward.
- Add a Focused/Show all scope control that uses normal Graph navigation rather than private component-only state.
- In Show all, create one card for every Issue in `allIssues`, including closed and disconnected Issues.
- Derive all parent and blocker links whose endpoints exist in `allIssues`, retaining the same direction, styling, anomaly, and parent-only layout rules as Focused.
- Show visible/total counts in both scopes.
- Entering Graph from another sidebar destination starts at Focused. Show all returns only when navigation returns to an entry that contains it; it is not a persisted preference.
- Exercise a representative 141-Issue/213-link fixture for deterministic construction, rendering, fit-to-view, and interaction responsiveness.

## Considerations

- Do not persist scope to settings or remember it independently of navigation.
- Do not add graph search, clustering, virtualization, alternate layout engines, or saved layouts.
- Disconnected cards are valid in Show all and need deterministic placement.
- The selected Issue field already belongs to the Graph destination contract but detailed selection behavior lands later.
- Keep React Flow attribution visible.
- A focused-empty graph may still offer Show all when closed Issues exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Focused remains the default whenever Graph is entered from another sidebar destination.
- [ ] Show all contains every Issue in `allIssues` exactly once, including closed and disconnected Issues.
- [ ] Show all renders every valid parent and blocker link with the established semantics.
- [ ] The scope control and visible/total counts clearly identify whether the graph is partial or complete.
- [ ] Back/Forward restores Graph scope exactly.
- [ ] Leaving Graph and later navigating back to its history entry restores that entry's scope; ordinary re-entry starts Focused.
- [ ] Empty Workspace and Focused-with-only-closed-Issues states offer accurate Show-all behavior.
- [ ] The representative dense fixture renders and remains interactive without an obvious lag regression.
- [ ] `mise run doctor:react` and `mise run verify` pass.

## Test Plan

- Pure graph-module tests comparing Focused and Show-all projections from the same fixture.
- Navigation tests for scope parsing, canonicalization, serialization, replacement, and Back/Forward restoration.
- UI tests for the scope control, counts, disconnected cards, empty/focused-empty states, and valid edges in Show all.
- A generated representative-size fixture asserts deterministic output and bounded render/interaction behavior without relying on exact machine timing.
- Run the canonical `mise run verify` gate.
title: Reveal every Issue with Show all
